verdict.rationale: First-party docs say AnythingLLM runs entirely on-device with no accounts or API keys. Hands-on reports confirm Ollama is detected automatically and that the tool works offline on an ordinary office PC. However, the evidence names only Ollama among the requested backends. llama.cpp appears only in a commenter's first impression, and LM Studio and vLLM are never mentioned. missing for 10: documented support for llama.cpp, LM Studio, and vLLM backends; first-party backend configuration docs covering local model providers.

support.subject: As a privacy-first user, I can run the assistant entirely on local models — Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio, or vLLM — with no cloud model dependency

citations.quote: A private AI assistant that runs entirely on your computer. No accounts, no API keys, no token limits.
With Ollama, everything was automatically detected, while manual setup is still possible.
this has been the only offline AI tool I've been able to install and start using on my standard office PC.
a no-fuss way to use LLMs both locally and via APIs
